column3: One event per logical connection the application releases, from SQLAlchemy's pool checkout and checkin (SqlTraceRecorder.checkoutConnection and releaseConnection, ConnectionPayload.java), also while the SQL Trace panel is paused, never for sharpit's own work, offered with the request id and thread current at checkout whichever thread releases it, a second release ignored, and only while the journal records connection (otherwise no pool listener runs and nothing is counted, as BootUI's checkoutConnection returns null); durationNanos is the held time, failedOrSlow is held at least the slow-query threshold, checkoutNanos is perf_counter_ns at checkout (the sql events' clock); not ported: the RuntimeEvent fields executionId and threadKind; deviation: waitNanos is always 0 (SQLAlchemy has no event for when the request for a connection began, and BootUI's readers treat 0 as no wait, so a wait is never invented); dataSource is the connection-pools panel's display name for the engine (never the URL or password), null for an engine the registry does not hold; the source counts as recorded only while the pool listener runs for the install; deviation (DEFAULT TAKEN, owner to confirm): statements is always -1, BootUI's unknown (the checkoutNanos convention), where BootUI's ConnectionCheckout.statementExecuted counts per execute: a per-statement count cost the SQL listener +1.5 us paired (no room), the recorder keeps no per-connection count to derive it at checkin, and only RequestJournalProfiles display text reads the field; a connection invalidated before its release offers no event; deviation: a pool that hands one record to several concurrent checkouts (StaticPool, SingletonThreadPool) journals one event for them, the last one's Deviation (sharpit-only text): when the listener is not armed (SQLAlchemy not imported or its listeners suspended) the source is shown as enabled-but-not-armed with its own reason, and a kind that reads it names that in its limitations, because BootUI has no listener that can be absent.

Ported from ConnectionsPerRequest.java:24-132 (intervals from checkoutNanos and durationNanos, a release before a checkout at one instant, one finding per route and data source, the hold-and-wait estimate with the pool size or P, same texts); deviations: a connection with no data source name or checkout time is counted apart and named in the check reason (BootUI skips it silently); not applicable when the exposure withheld every request id; the pool size is a queue pool's size plus overflow (BootUI reads Hikari's maximum), unknown for another pool or an unbounded overflow Deviation (sharpit-only text): a pool that hands one connection to every checkout (StaticPool, SingletonThreadPool) is named in the reason, so a clean result on in-memory sqlite does not read as proof of no nesting.

Adds one limitation when a route's warm requests hold connection events (deviation, proposed): a wait for a pooled connection is not measured, because SQLAlchemy reports none and the connection event's waitNanos is always 0, so it stays in the span it happened in (BootUI shows a connection-wait phase); w5c-K1's row otherwise stands
